Independent Bézout and dual-incidence derivation in this audit
correctness.rationale: The cited inequalities apply to degree 9 with these singularities. Nearly-free exponents must be (4,5), so τ=47. The pairwise intersection degree 32 and the Tjurina sum imply t+n3=15 and n2+n3=2. The published inequality then reads 134+ n2 ≥134+10n2 after multiplying by four, so only (0,13,2) remains. Independently, a conic transverse to the line has two distinct transverse contacts, and without nodes these must be the two triple points. With no triple on the line, all four conics are tangent to it. With two triples on it, exactly the same two conics go through both triples, and the other two are tangent to the line. One triple on the line is impossible. For two conics with two tacnodes, their dual conics meet with at least order two at each corresponding tangent (dual tangents encode the common original point); Bézout exhausts the common tangent lines. Using one as an arrangement line gives a forbidden three-branch contact. Therefore in the zero-triple case the total tacnodes are at most 4+6=10, and in the two-triple case they are at most 2+1+1+4·2=12 (the pair through the triples and the line-tangent pair each contribute at most one). Neither attains thirteen.
residual_risks: The arithmetic checker tests necessary inequalities and bounds only; the geometric argument proves the complex nonexistence.
